title: DK Bond Tracker Test Plan Addendum — Add-Position Flow and Active-Position Lock (FR-25/FR-26)
change_record: Addendum v1.0 after owner decisions D14/D15 (2026-10-30): adds FR-25 (single add-position flow, one bonds master row) and FR-26 (strict active-position lock on normalized company name OR ISIN, HARD BLOCK, release on Completed, re-buy re-locks) as TC-59..TC-66; the combined suite (v1 TC-01..TC-58 plus this addendum) becomes 44-requirement coverage (42 legacy + FR-25 + FR-26); no legacy test case or binding is altered.
scope: Verification of FR-25 and FR-26 only, as added by the PRD/SRS addendum after D14/D15. In scope: Watch List add form single submission producing exactly one bonds master row rendered by grid, dashboard and watch list; duplicate blocking on normalized company name (trim/case-insensitive) OR ISIN against active (On-going or Danger) positions; named-error block message shape; lock release on Completed (D5: months paid >= tenure); re-buy starting On-going and re-locks; no override and no force-accept path. Out of scope: anything owned by Test_Plan_DK_Bond_Tracker_v1 (TC-01..TC-58, FR-01..FR-24, NFR, DATA, ledger L1 caveat).
approach: Same pytest posture as v1. Unit cases exercise the lock key normalization and the named-error message builder against pure functions with temp SQLite fixtures; integration cases drive the add-form submit path (Flask test client) against a seeded database and assert the bonds master row count plus per-surface reads; the lock-release/re-lock lifecycle cases seed ledger rows to move a position through Completed via the D5 status engine and re-attempt the add at each step. Every addendum case is LOCAL and planned; no REMOTE case is needed because nothing here requires a second OS or machine.

strategy.local: All addendum TCs (TC-59..TC-66) run as pytest from the project root: unit cases on lock-key normalization and block-message shape, integration/e2e cases via the Flask test client against temp seeded SQLite databases, including the Completed-release and re-buy re-lock lifecycle driven through the D5 status engine.

test_cases.title: Add form happy path: one submit creates one bonds row rendered by grid, watch list and dashboard
test_cases.steps:
1. Start from an empty portfolio and open the Watch List add form.
2. Submit company, ISIN, amount, tenure and start month exactly once.
3. Count rows in the bonds master table.
4. Render the monthly grid, the dashboard and the watch list.
5. Compare the position details shown on each surface against the submitted values and against the single bonds row.
test_cases.expected: Exactly one new bonds master row exists; the monthly grid, dashboard and watch list all display that position from the same row with the submitted values; no surface prompts for or stores a second copy of the company/position details; the total bond count increases by exactly 1 (FR-25 AC1 and AC2).

test_cases.title: Duplicate company name (case/whitespace variant) is HARD BLOCKED with named error
test_cases.steps: 1. Insert active position company='Beta Finance', ISIN='IN1234567890', status On-going. 2. POST add-position with company='  BETA FINANCE  ' (case + whitespace variant), ISIN='IN9999999999' (different). 3. Assert no row inserted. 4. Assert response contains the named error. Note: candidate is a pure case/whitespace variant of the same name with a DIFFERENT ISIN, so only the name key can match (equality after trim+lowercase).
test_cases.expected: Add rejected with 'Cannot add position: Beta Finance has an active position (On-going)' (name key matched despite different ISIN); bonds count unchanged; no override path exercised

test_cases.title: Duplicate ISIN with a different company name is HARD BLOCKED
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed an active position 'Beta Finance' (On-going) with ISIN 'IN1234567890'.
2. Submit the add form with company 'MMF Investments' and ISIN 'in1234567890' (case-variant ISIN, entirely different name).
3. Capture the response, error text and bonds master row count.
test_cases.expected: The add is HARD BLOCKED because the ISIN match blocks even though the company names differ; the named error identifies the active Beta Finance position and its status; no new bonds row is written.

test_cases.title: Both keys match (normalized name AND ISIN): still a single HARD BLOCK with named error
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed an active position 'Beta Finance' (On-going) with ISIN 'IN1234567890'.
2. Evaluate the lock check for a candidate with company ' BETA FINANCE ' and ISIN 'in1234567890' — both the normalized name and the ISIN match the same active position.
3. Capture the block decision, the named error and any duplicate-error behavior.
test_cases.expected: The candidate is HARD BLOCKED exactly once with a named error naming the blocking position and its status; the both-match case produces no double error, no bypass, and no ambiguity about which position blocks — either match alone is sufficient and both matching changes nothing.

test_cases.title: Completed position releases the lock: the next add succeeds
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed the 'Beta Finance' position (On-going) and confirm an add attempt is blocked.
2. Record ledger payments until months paid >= tenure so the D5 status engine reports Completed.
3. Submit a new Beta Finance position via the add form.
4. Verify the new row and its computed status.
test_cases.expected: With the existing position Completed the add is ALLOWED (lock released only by Completed per D5, months paid >= tenure); exactly one new bonds row exists and its status computes as On-going; no named-error block is raised for the previously blocking company.

test_cases.title: Re-buy after Completed starts On-going and re-locks: a further add is blocked again
test_cases.steps:
1. Complete TC-63's flow: prior Beta Finance position Completed, new Beta Finance position added and computing On-going.
2. Immediately submit another Beta Finance add (name or ISIN variant).
3. Capture the block, the named error and the bonds master row count.
test_cases.expected: The re-bought position starts On-going and re-locks the company: the further add is HARD BLOCKED with a named error identifying the new active position and its status; no third bonds row is written; the lock holds until the new position too completes.

test_cases.title: Block message content matches the SRS AC shape exactly
test_cases.steps:
1. Build the block error for active position 'Beta Finance' with computed status On-going.
2. Compare the message against the SRS AC shape: 'Cannot add position: Beta Finance has an active position (On-going)'.
3. Repeat with a Danger-status active position and verify the status token reflects Danger.
4. Verify the message is surfaced to the user, not swallowed by a handler.
test_cases.expected: The message matches the SRS AC shape exactly — prefix 'Cannot add position:', then the blocking company name, then 'has an active position (', then the computed status, then ')' — with the real company name and live D5 status substituted; a Danger blocker is named as Danger; the message is surfaced visibly per FR-21 and never logged-and-swallowed.

test_cases.title: No override: an add attempt with a force flag/param is still rejected
test_cases.steps:
1. Seed an active Beta Finance position (On-going).
2. Submit the add form with a force/override flag or parameter set truthy (for example force=true, override=true, confirm_anyway=1) while the lock matches.
3. Capture the response, error text and bonds master row count.
4. Inspect the add path for any code branch that honors a force or override input.
test_cases.expected: The force/override attempt is rejected with the same HARD BLOCK named error naming the active position and its status; no bonds row is written under any flag value; the add path contains no force-accept or override branch — enforcement has no override, per FR-26 and D15.
